current_trade_scale: 34.9 Mt total trade FY25; $73.5b international cargo
declared_or_observed_capacity: Vision 2060 projects ~5m+ TEU annually; ~200ha Future Port Expansion area
rail_and_intermodal_role: Brisbane Multimodal Terminal; interstate rail via Acacia Ridge; only 2.1% of containers moved by rail in FY25
primary_catchment_or_network_role: Queensland / SEQ gateway with statewide agricultural and industrial hinterland
expansion_or_optionality: ~200ha Future Port Expansion; dedicated freight rail to port remains a major future enabling option
notes: Container growth is strong but current rail mode share is low; do not treat port rail connection as equivalent to high-capacity dedicated freight rail.

current_trade_scale: 2.82m TEU FY25; 5.08 Mt bulk liquids/gas FY25
declared_or_observed_capacity: >7m TEU current port capacity; future forecast >7.3m TEU by 2056
rail_and_intermodal_role: On-dock rail at all 3 container terminals; direct dedicated freight rail to Enfield, Moorebank and Cooks River; long-term rail target 3m TEU/year
primary_catchment_or_network_role: Greater Sydney plus regional NSW exports; ~80% of import containers travel <=40km and ~90% of containers <=50km
expansion_or_optionality: Staged on-dock rail expansion; fourth container terminal unlikely before 2045
notes: Large latent terminal capacity already exists; landside rail/intermodal capacity is the more important growth variable.

current_trade_scale: Major vehicle, bulk, project and industrial cargo gateway
declared_or_observed_capacity: Future NSW container terminal has concept approval; timing linked to Port Botany growth
rail_and_intermodal_role: Rail-connected; Maldon-Dombarton / SWIRL and Outer Sydney Orbital would materially improve access to Western Sydney
primary_catchment_or_network_role: Illawarra, southern/western Sydney and regional NSW; handles 100% of NSW motor vehicle imports
expansion_or_optionality: Government-designated future container augmentation to Port Botany; substantial value depends on future freight links
notes: Treat future container role as approved strategic optionality, not operating container capacity.

current_trade_scale: Capacity stated as >200 Mt cargo annually and 10,000 ship movements; ~$48b trade enabled annually
declared_or_observed_capacity: Deepwater shipping channel reported operating at ~50% capacity; significant port land available
rail_and_intermodal_role: Direct national road/rail access; strong bulk freight inheritance
primary_catchment_or_network_role: Hunter, northern NSW and national export supply chains
expansion_or_optionality: Large physical spare capacity and trade-diversification program; RoRo capability added; container expansion remains a separate policy/commercial question
notes: Exceptional physical spare-capacity signal should not be converted into assumed container-market capacity without separate legal, commercial and terminal evidence.

declared_or_observed_capacity: Container trade expected to double over ~30 years; next capacity stage planned at Webb Dock North
rail_and_intermodal_role: Port Rail Transformation Project operational; new Coode Road terminal with two 600m sidings; Webb Dock freight-link/rail terminal planning remains future work
primary_catchment_or_network_role: Victoria and south-east Australia container gateway
expansion_or_optionality: Port Capacity Enhancement Program targets Webb Dock North new capacity around 2036 subject to approvals; 29ha former market site added to port estate
notes: Separate completed Swanson rail improvements from future Webb Dock rail access and container-terminal expansion.

current_trade_scale: 13.6m+ tonnes cargo annually; $10.2b+ trade; 1,060 vessel visits
declared_or_observed_capacity: 15 berths across Corio Quay and Lascelles; 90+ ha port land
rail_and_intermodal_role: Road and rail links serving Geelong and south-west Victoria supply chains
primary_catchment_or_network_role: Regional Victoria bulk, energy, agriculture, construction and project-cargo gateway
expansion_or_optionality: 2024 Port Development Strategy plans capacity, transport corridors and land needs for regional catchments
notes: Important regional counterpoint to Melbourne: high bulk/industrial role but not a substitute container gateway by default.
